promptLatex: Triangle $T$ has area $36$. A second triangle is similar to $T$ with every side $3$ times as long. What is the area of the second triangle?
hintLatex: Areas of similar figures are not in the same ratio as their sides.
The area scales with the square of the length ratio.
solutionLatex:
The two triangles are similar with scale factor $k = 3$, since every side of the second is three times the matching side of the first.

For similar triangles the area ratio is $k^2$, not $k$, because area is a length squared. Here $k^2 = 9$.

The second triangle therefore has area $36 \cdot 9 = 324$.
